{{Short description|Line between midpoints of 2 diagonals in a 4-sided shape other than a parallelogram}}
{{distinguish|Newton-Gauss line|Isaac Newton line}}
[[File:Newton line.svg|thumb|upright=1.5|{{mvar|E, K, F}} lie on a common line, the Newton line]]

In [[Euclidean geometry]], the '''Newton line''' is the line that connects the midpoints of the two [[diagonal]]s in a [[convex polygon|convex]] [[quadrilateral]] other than a [[parallelogram]].{{r|alsina}}

==Properties==
The [[line segment]]s {{mvar|{{overline|GH}}}} and {{mvar|{{overline|IJ}}}} that connect the midpoints of opposite sides (the [[bimedian]]s) of a convex quadrilateral intersect in a point that lies on the Newton line. This point {{mvar|K}} bisects the line segment {{mvar|{{overline|EF}}}} that connects the diagonal midpoints.{{r|alsina}}

By [[Anne's theorem]] and its converse, any interior point ''P'' on the Newton line of a quadrilateral {{mvar|ABCD}} has the property that
:<math>[\triangle ABP] + [\triangle CDP] = [\triangle ADP] + [\triangle BCP],</math>
where {{math|[△{{mvar|ABP}}]}} denotes the area of triangle {{math|△{{mvar|ABP}}}}.{{sfnp|Alsina|Nelsen|2010|pp=[https://books.google.com/books?id=mIT5-BN_L0oC&pg=PA116 116&ndash;117]}}

If the quadrilateral is a [[tangential quadrilateral]], then its [[incenter]] also lies on this line.{{r|vic}}
